extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants / patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when a final rejection (including first-action final) is proper, when finality must be withdrawn, timing for replies and extensions, examiner actions (advisory actions and examiner's amendments), and transitional after-final procedures under 37 CFR 1.129 and related rules (MPEP § 706.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph usage limitation when new ground of rejection introduced
rubrics_metrics.description: This form paragraph should not be used, and a final rejection is improper, where there is another new ground of rejection introduced by the examiner that was not necessitated by amendment to the claims nor based on information submitted in an information disclosure statement filed during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make a final rejection using the form paragraph if the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection that is not a consequence of applicant amendment or an IDS timely filed with the appropriate fee. (Original wording preserved.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Is Final when joint research agreement prior-art disqualification submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant’s submission of the requirements for the joint research agreement prior art disqualification under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(c) on [1] prompted the new double patenting rejection presented in this Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.40.02.fti when the applicant's submission under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) necessitates the new ground of rejection; remind applicant of extension of time policy (37 CFR 1.136(a)). Insert filing date of the submission in bracket 1. Do not use if another new ground was introduced not necessitated by amendment/IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for making first action final in a continuing or substitute application
rubrics_metrics.description: For a new application, claims may be finally rejected in the first Office action when (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims of the new application (1) are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with, the claims in the earlier application ... and (2) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both prongs A and B must be met to make a first-action final in a continuation/substitute file. This prevents improper finality where claims or context changed such that earlier prosecution would not have supported final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for making first action final after an RCE (37 CFR 1.114)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application in which an RCE has been filed, claims may be finally rejected in the first action following the filing of the RCE ... when all the claims in the application after the entry of the submission under 37 CFR 1.114 and any entered supplemental amendments (A) are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with the claims in the application prior to the entry of the submission under 37 CFR 1.114 ... and (B) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the application prior to the filing of the RCE under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RCE cannot be used to switch inventions; condition (A) is always met where the RCE is accompanied by a submission that will be entered as a matter of right. If claims are independent and distinct from previously examined claims, an RCE cannot be used to obtain continued examination on those claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper to make first-action final when material was denied entry in parent application due to raising new issues or new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action in a continuing or substitute application where that application contains material which was presented in the earlier application after final rejection or closing of prosecution but was denied entry because (A) new issues were raised that required further consideration and/or search, or (B) the issue of new matter was raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly applies after filing of an RCE where material previously denied entry raised new issues/new matter. These circumstances preclude first-action finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper to make first-action final in continuation-in-part with new subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action in a continuation-in-part application where any claim includes subject matter not present in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CIP claims include new matter absent from the parent, do not make first-action final on that ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for interview prior to first action in continuing/substitute application
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an interview prior to first action on a continuing or substitute application should ordinarily be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should normally grant such interview requests before issuing first office action in continuing/substitute applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs to use for first action final rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: A first action final rejection should be made by using Form Paragraphs 7.41 or 7.41.03, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specified form paragraphs (7.41 for general first-action final; 7.41.03 for CPA in a design application) and precede with appropriate form paragraphs 2.30 or 2.35 as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.41 Action Is Final, First Action (template conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a [1] of applicant’s earlier Application No. [2]. All claims are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with the invention claimed in the earlier application ... Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action in this case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bracket insertions as directed; remind applicant of extension of time policy (37 CFR 1.136(a)). Form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 2.30 or 2.35 as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prematureness of final rejection — procedural challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Any question as to prematureness of a final rejection should be raised, if at all, while the application is still pending before the primary examiner. This is purely a question of practice, wholly distinct from the tenability of the rejection. It may therefore not be advanced as a ground for appeal, or made the basis of complaint before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board. It is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenges to prematureness must be raised administratively (petition under 1.181) while pending; cannot be appealed on that ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality when final rejection is premature
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on request by applicant for reconsideration, the primary examiner finds the final rejection to have been premature, he or she should withdraw the finality of the rejection. The finality of the Office action must be withdrawn while the application is still pending. The examiner cannot withdraw the final rejection once the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form paragraph 7.42 when withdrawing finality of the rejection of the last Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule for withdrawal of a final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered ... it should not be withdrawn at the applicant’s or patent owner’s request except on a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b). Further amendment or argument will be considered in certain instances. An amendment that will place the application either in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal may be admitted. Also, amendments complying with objections or requirements as to form are to be permitted after final action in accordance with 37 CFR 1.116(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may withdraw the rejection if new facts or reasons convince the examiner that previously rejected claims are allowable, or to apply a new ground of rejection where a new reference fully meets a claim or meets it except for differences shown to be completely obvious. Limit practice: do not withdraw to apply subsidiary/cumulative references or references merely 'better than' those of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited circumstances to withdraw final rejection to apply a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Although it is permissible to withdraw a final rejection for the purpose of entering a new ground of rejection, this practice is to be limited to situations where a new reference either fully meets at least one claim or meets it except for differences which are shown to be completely obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally withdraw with respect to the claim(s) involved. See MPEP § 1207.03 for what may constitute a new ground of rejection. Do not use for subsidiary/cumulative references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for reply to a final rejection — shortened statutory periods and variable reply rule
rubrics_metrics.description: All final rejections setting a 3-month shortened statutory period (SSP) for reply should contain one of form paragraphs ... advising applicant that if the first reply is filed within 2 months of the date of the final Office action, the shortened statutory period will expire at 3 months from the date of the final rejection or on the date the advisory action is mailed, whichever is later. In no event can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the mailing date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variable reply period: if first reply filed within 2 months, SSP expires at 3 months or when advisory action mailed (whichever later). Saturdays/Sundays/DC federal holidays rules per 37 CFR 1.7(a). Procedure does not apply to SSP less than 3 months (e.g., reissue litigation, reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory action examiner determinations after a timely first reply (within 2 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action sets a variable reply period ... AND applicant files a complete first reply to the final Office action within 2 months ... the examiner must determine if the reply: (1) places the application in condition for allowance; (2) places the application in condition for allowance except for matters of form which the examiner can change without authorization; or (3) does not place the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If (1) or (2), process as allowance and no extension fees due. If (3), advisory action should inform applicant that the SSP for reply expires 3 months from the date of the final rejection or as of the mailing date of the advisory action, whichever is later, by checking box 1.b) on PTOL-303.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when applicant does NOT file a complete first reply within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action sets a variable reply period ... and applicant does NOT file a complete first reply to the examiner's final Office action within 2 months, the examiner should check box 1.a) at the top portion of the Advisory Action form, PTOL-303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When box 1.b) is checked (i.e., applicant did timely file), the time for applicant to take further action (including calculation of extension fees) begins to run 3 months from the date of final rejection or from the date of the advisory action, whichever is later. Extension fees cannot be prorated and statutory period for reply cannot exceed 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments after timely first reply (within 2 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has been filed within 2 months of the final Office action, an examiner’s amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without the payment of extension fees even if the examiner’s amendment is made more than 3 months from the date of the final Office action. Note that an examiner’s amendment may not be made more than 6 months from the date of the final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may place application in condition for allowance by amendment without extension fees if first reply was timely (<=2 months). But examiner's amendment cannot be made after 6 months from final rejection mailing (app would be abandoned).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments when first reply not filed within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has not been filed within 2 months of the final Office action, applicant’s authorization to make an amendment to place the application in condition for allowance must be made either within the 3 month shortened statutory period or within an extended period for reply that has been petitioned and paid for by applicant pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: examiner's amendment correcting only formal matters identified for the first time after a reply to a final would not require extension fee if the prior reply put the application in condition for allowance except for correction of such formal matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) — requirements and authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires a petition for an extension and the appropriate fee provided for in 37 CFR 1.17. Where an extension of time is necessary to place an application in condition for allowance ... applicant may file the required petition and fee or give authorization to the examiner to make the petition of record and charge a specified fee to a deposit account. Office employees may not accept oral (telephonic) instructions to complete the Credit Card Payment Form or otherwise charge a patent process fee to a credit card.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization must be of record in an examiner’s amendment indicating the name of person authorizing, when authorized, deposit account number, length of extension requested, and amount to be charged. Use Form Paragraph 13.02.02 for authorization template. In no case can any extension carry the date for reply beyond six months (35 U.S.C. 133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 13.02.02 — Extension of Time and Examiner’s Amendment Authorized (template)
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) is required in order to make an examiner’s amendment that places this application in condition for allowance. During a conversation conducted on [1], [2] requested an extension of time for [3] MONTH(S) and authorized the Director to charge Deposit Account No. [4] the required fee of $ [5] for this extension and authorized the following examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this paragraph to document applicant authorization for examiner to file petition/fee for extension and effectuate examiner's amendment; specify that any unacceptable changes can be amended as provided by 37 CFR 1.312 and must be submitted no later than payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice after final: replies, consideration, interviews, and formal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should be processed and considered promptly by all Office personnel. Replies after final should not be considered by the examiner unless they are filed within the SSP or are accompanied by a petition for an extension of time and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17 and 37 CFR 1.136(a)). Interviews may be conducted after the expiration of the shortened statutory period for reply but within the 6-month statutory period for reply without the payment of an extension fee. Formal matters identified for the first time after a reply to a final Office action and that require action by applicant to correct may be required in an Ex parte Quayle action if the application is otherwise in condition for allowance. No extension fees would be required in that case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process replies after final promptly; ensure petition/fee when outside SSP. Interviews allowed after SSP expiration but before 6 months without extension fee; Ex parte Quayle actions may be used to correct formal matters identified post-reply without extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality when prosecution is reopened after a final reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is to be reopened after a final Office action has been replied to, the finality of the previous Office action should be withdrawn to avoid the issue of abandonment and the payment of extension fees. For example, if a new reference comes to the attention of the examiner which renders unpatentable a claim indicated to be allowable, the Office action should begin with a statement to the effect: 'The finality of the Office action mailed is hereby withdrawn in view of the new ground of rejection set forth below.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form paragraph 7.42 in addition to this statement if appropriate. Withdrawal avoids abandonment and unnecessary extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional after-final practice under 37 CFR 1.129(a) — eligibility and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant in an application ... that has been pending for at least two years as of June 8, 1995 ... is entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits after final rejection ... if the first submission and the fee set forth in § 1.17(r) are filed prior to the filing of an appeal brief and prior to abandonment of the application. The finality of the final rejection is automatically withdrawn upon the timely filing of the submission and payment of the fee set forth in § 1.17(r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission includes IDS, amendment to specification/claims/drawings, new substantive argument, or new evidence; no amendment resulting from payment of fee may introduce new matter (35 U.S.C. 132). The transitional after-final practice applies only to applications filed on or before June 8, 1995 (and other date-specific requirements described). Use form paragraph 7.41.01.fti to notify applicant of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and treatment of IDS and other submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any IDS submitted under 37 CFR 1.129(a) on or after June 8, 2005 without a statement specified in 37 CFR 1.97(e) will be treated as though it had been filed within the time period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p). The examiner may introduce a new ground of rejection based on the information submitted in the IDS and make the next Office action final provided that the examiner introduces no other new ground of rejection which has not been necessitated by amendment to the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submission under 1.129(a) is not fully responsive, give applicant a shortened statutory period of TWO MONTHS to submit a complete reply (use form paragraph 7.42.02.fti). Timely payment of 1.17(r) fee automatically withdraws finality and causes previously unentered/conditional submissions to be entered in order filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of nonresponsive submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The timely submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) filed on [1] is not fully responsive to the prior Office action because [2]. Since the submission appears to be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to the prior Office action, applicant is given a shortened statutory period of TWO MONTHS from the mailing date of this letter to submit a complete reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If nonresponsive, issue form paragraph 7.42.02.fti with reasons in bracket 2; this supersedes prior SSP and may be extended under 1.136(a). Payment of 1.17(r) prior to appeal filing may be construed as request to dismiss appeal and continue prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: First action final following submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) filed prior to June 8, 2005
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission and payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r), the next Office action on the merits may be made final only under the conditions for making a first action in a continuing application final set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.03.fti may be used to make the first action final following a submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) filed prior to June 8, 2005; ensure claims are drawn to same invention and could have been finally rejected on grounds of record if entered prior to entry under 1.129(a).
